name: RRB JE
fullName: Railway Recruitment Boards – Junior Engineer, Depot Material Superintendent & Chemical and Metallurgical Assistant
approxCandidates: ≈10–12 lakh applicants per cycle (approx.; CEN 04/2026 figure not yet published)
eligibility: Diploma/Degree in the relevant engineering discipline (B.Sc. with Physics & Chemistry for CMA); 18–33 yrs as on 1 Jan 2027 (relaxation as per rules)

notification.summary: CEN 04/2026 notified Level-6 JE, DMS and CMA posts (≈4,098 in the short notice; revised to 4,029 by an 18 Aug 2026 corrigendum as reported). Applications ran from 14 Aug to 13 Sep 2026. An RRB notice dated 16 Sep 2026 tentatively schedules CBT 1 on 27, 28 and 30 October 2026, with city slips ≈10 days and e-call letters ≈4 days before the allotted date. (The Feb 2026 CBT dates seen online belong to the earlier CEN 05/2025 cycle.)

pattern.notes: CBT 1 is common to all JE/DMS/CMA posts and is qualifying/screening only (marks not counted in final merit); normalised scores are used to shortlist ≈15× vacancies for the discipline-specific CBT 2. 1/3 negative marking. Qualifying %: UR/EWS 40%, OBC/SC 30%, ST 25%. General Science is of Class 10 (CBSE) level.

trendAnalysis.summary: JE CBT 1 shifts of Dec 2024 (CEN 03/2024) and early 2026 (CEN 05/2025) were rated moderate. Mathematics is the longest section, with algebraic identities, trigonometry, mensuration (3-D solids), CI and speed problems; it is a notch above Group D level. Reasoning features coding, series, blood relations, syllogism, puzzles and data sufficiency. General Science (30 Q) is the scoring area for engineering aspirants – physics numericals on motion, electricity and optics plus NCERT chemistry and biology. GA (15 Q) mixes current affairs with polity, history and science-tech. Good attempts are around 75–85.

topics.topic: Physics: Units, Motion & Laws of Motion

pyqBlueprint.method: Compiled from the two latest JE CBT 1 cycles: CEN 03/2024 (CBT 1 held 16–18 Dec 2024) and CEN 05/2025 (CBT 1 held 19, 20 and 25 Feb 2026, per the RRB exam notices). No JE CBT 1 was held in 2025. RRB bars sharing of live questions, so web searches (Oct 2026) returned only difficulty/good-attempt analyses (SSCAdda, Physics Wallah, MADE EASY) with topic weightage – e.g. series 4–5, analogy and classification 3–5, coding and seating 3–4 per shift. Question TYPES were described from those lists and the writer's own knowledge of the released 2019 and 2024 JE CBT 1 papers/response sheets; WebFetch of the papers was not possible. All patterns are paraphrased.

archetypes.pattern: Remainder of a large power or product using cyclicity/modular patterns
Number of factors, divisibility, largest/smallest n-digit number divisible by k
BODMAS with mixed fractions and brackets
Square roots of decimals and surd simplification using a given value (√2, √3, √5)
HCF × LCM = product, bells ringing together, least number with given remainders
Compound/chain ratios (A:B, B:C, C:D → A:D) and division in a ratio
Ages: ratio now and some years ago/hence, or sum of ages with a past/future condition
Elections, income–expenditure–savings and successive percentage change
Chain of sales with successive profit/loss, or CP/SP from profit %
Mark-up and discount combined; successive discounts
Compound interest (annual/half-yearly) – amount, principal or CI
Simple interest: amounts after two different periods → rate/principal
Men–women equivalence, efficiency and combined work
Pipes filling with a leak or an outlet pipe
Trains crossing a man/platform/each other – speed or length
Boats and streams, average speed
3-D solids: cube/cuboid/cylinder/cone/sphere/hemisphere volume, surface area, recasting into smaller solids
2-D figures: rhombus/trapezium/circle/triangle area and perimeter
Identities with x + 1/x, surds (x = a + √b), a³ ± b³ – find higher powers
Linear equations in two variables and value of an expression
Polygon interior/exterior angles, triangle centres and circle theorems
Trigonometric identities and ratio evaluation (sec θ + tan θ, sin θ + cos θ conditions)
Heights and distances with 30°/45°/60° angles of elevation/depression
Mean, median and mode of a small data set

Word-pair analogy: identify the relation in the first pair (instrument–quantity measured, worker–tool/workplace, organ–function, product–raw material) and pick the term that completes the second pair; distractors share the category but not the relation

Number or letter-cluster analogy: first pair linked by n² ± k, n³, n(n+1) or a fixed letter shift; apply the same rule to the third term; distractors come from the neighbouring rule (n² vs n²+1, etc.)
Number series – find the next/missing term; rules are increasing differences, ×n ± k, squares/cubes or primes; distractors are values from applying the rule with an off-by-one step
Letter or letter-cluster series: each letter in a cluster moves by a fixed/increasing step (+2, +3 …) or skips letters; choose the next cluster; distractors miss one letter shift
Letter-shift coding: a word is coded by shifting each letter (+k, alternating ±k, position-based shift or reverse + shift); find the code of a new word or decode a code
Number/position coding: word coded as sum or product of alphabet positions or reverse positions, or common-word sentence codes; find the code of a new word
Symbol substitution: + − × ÷ (or letters) are re-defined; substitute and evaluate with BODMAS; distractors come from left-to-right evaluation
Interchange two signs (or numbers) to make an equation correct, or find the hidden rule of a defined operation (e.g. a # b = a² + b²) and apply it
Pointing/introduction statement (e.g. "only son of my father's …") – decode the chain to name the relation; gender trap built into distractors
Coded relations (A + B means A is mother of B …) or a family chain of 4–6 people – find how X is related to Y or which expression is true
Two or three categorical statements (All/Some/No) followed by two conclusions; pick Only I / Only II / Both / Neither; traps are reverse "All" conversions and possibility cases
Arrange 4–5 words in dictionary order (or a logical/meaningful sequence) and report the word at a given position or the correct order
Choose the Venn relationship (disjoint, one inside another, partial overlap) that best represents three given classes
Two-set counting: totals, "both" and "neither" figures given – find only-A / neither / both
Data sufficiency: a question with Statement I and II – decide whether I alone, II alone, either, both together or neither is sufficient
Short everyday statement (railway/civic/public notice) with two conclusions or courses of action – select which logically follow
Odd one out among four words from a common category (planets, units, instruments, organs) where one breaks the property
Odd number / number-pair / letter-cluster out: three follow a numeric rule (prime, n:n², fixed gap) and one does not
Linear row of 5–7 people facing north/south with immediate-left/right and "between" clues – find who sits at a position or between two people
Ranking/comparison: position from both ends of a row/class, or ordering by height/weight/marks from comparative statements
Circular table seating (facing centre) or day/floor scheduling with 5–6 entities – identify neighbour/position
Walk path with left/right turns and distances – find the shortest distance and direction from the start (Pythagoras triples)
Facing direction after a series of clockwise/anticlockwise turns, or shadow-based direction at sunrise/sunset
Statement (notice/advertisement/advice) with two assumptions – decide which are implicit
Should-type policy statement with Yes/No arguments – decide which arguments are strong
Mirror/water image of a letter–number string or clock time, or counting triangles/squares in a simple figure

archetypes.topic: Physics: Units, Motion & Laws of Motion
archetypes.pattern: Equations of motion numericals (v = u + at, s = ut + ½at², v² = u² + 2as, free fall with g = 10 m/s²); distractors from forgetting ½ or using wrong sign

archetypes.topic: Physics: Units, Motion & Laws of Motion
archetypes.pattern: SI units, scalar vs vector, and Newton's laws concepts (inertia, action–reaction examples)

archetypes.topic: Physics: Units, Motion & Laws of Motion
archetypes.pattern: Momentum / F = ma / impulse numericals with unit conversion (g → kg, km/h → m/s)
Work, kinetic/potential energy and power numericals (W = Fs, KE = ½mv², PE = mgh, P = W/t) including "velocity doubled → KE ×4" type
Gravitation: universal law (effect of changing distance/mass), g on Moon, mass vs weight, free fall
Mirror/lens formula numericals: image distance, magnification, R = 2f; sign-convention traps in options
Refraction: refractive index and speed of light, power of lens P = 1/f (in metres), lens type from sign
Natural optical phenomena (scattering, total internal reflection, dispersion, twinkling) and defects of vision with correcting lens
Ohm's law and series/parallel resistance combinations – find equivalent resistance or current
Electric power and energy: P = VI = V²/R, kWh consumption and cost, heating effect (H = I²Rt)
Magnetic effects: Fleming's rules, right-hand thumb rule, motor vs generator, field lines, fuse/earthing
Wave numericals: v = fλ, time period, echo distance (2d = vt)
Properties of sound (audible range, infrasonic/ultrasonic, speed in media) and heat/temperature scale conversions
Atomic structure: protons/neutrons/electrons from Z and A, electronic configuration (K, L, M), valency, isotopes/isobars
Periodic table: group/period of an element from its configuration, trends in atomic size/metallic character, Döbereiner/Newlands/Mendeleev facts
Mole concept and molecular mass; states of matter, sublimation/evaporation concepts
Common salts – chemical formula/name/use of baking soda, washing soda, bleaching powder, Plaster of Paris, gypsum
pH scale and indicators (litmus, phenolphthalein, methyl orange), neutralisation and everyday acids
Metals: reactivity series & displacement, ores and extraction, alloys and their constituents, corrosion/rancidity
Carbon compounds: homologous series formula (CₙH₂ₙ₊₂ etc.), functional groups, IUPAC names, allotropes of carbon
Identify the type of reaction (combination, decomposition, displacement, double displacement, redox) from an equation
Oxidation–reduction: substance oxidised/reduced, oxidising agent; balancing coefficients
Diseases and their causative agents, vaccines, vitamin/mineral deficiency diseases
Human organ systems: digestive enzymes and organs, blood components, heart chambers, nervous system/brain parts, hormones
Plant life processes: photosynthesis requirements, xylem/phloem, transpiration, plant hormones and their functions
Mendel's monohybrid/dihybrid ratios, sex determination, evolution terms (homologous/analogous organs), food chains and ozone
Sports events of the last year – winner, host city, venue
Awards and appointments in the news (Nobel, national awards, constitutional posts)
Government schemes and summits – objective, beneficiaries, launch year
INC sessions, movements and their places/years
Ancient and medieval dynasties, rulers and monuments
Parliament and President – procedures, presiding officers, powers
Constitutional Articles and landmark amendments
Rivers (east/west flowing), soils, crops and physical features
Budget, taxation (GST) and RBI/banking concepts
ISRO launch vehicles/missions and indigenous defence platforms
Classical dances, festivals and sports terms matched with states/games
Indian Railways firsts, new lines/trains and static GK (HQs, days)

resources.notes: Question papers with provisional answer keys and response sheets are published by RRBs only during the post-exam objection window via regional RRB websites (e.g. https://www.rrbcdg.gov.in, linked from https://www.rrbapply.gov.in). No permanent official archive; memory-based papers from coaching publishers are unofficial.

questions.question: What is the remainder when 2³¹ is divided by 5?
How many positive factors (divisors) does 360 have?
What is the value of √0.0169?
Three bells ring at intervals of 12, 18 and 30 minutes. If they ring together at 8:00 a.m., when will they next ring together?
The sum of the present ages of a father and his son is 56 years. Four years ago, the father's age was three times the son's age. What is the father's present age?
questions.explanation: Let son = s, father = 56 − s. Then 52 − s = 3(s − 4) ⇒ 4s = 64 ⇒ s = 16. Father = 40 years.

questions.question: In an election between two candidates, the winner got 58% of the valid votes and won by 2,400 votes. What was the total number of valid votes?
A sells an article to B at a profit of 20%, and B sells it to C at a loss of 10%. If C pays ₹5,400, what was A's cost price?
A sum amounts to ₹13,310 in 3 years at 10% per annum compound interest (compounded annually). What is the sum?
4 men or 6 women can finish a work in 15 days. In how many days will 2 men and 6 women together finish it?
questions.explanation: 4 men = 6 women ⇒ 1 man = 1.5 women. 2 men + 6 women = 9 women. Work = 6 × 15 = 90 woman-days ⇒ 90/9 = 10 days.

questions.question: Two pipes can fill a tank separately in 20 minutes and 30 minutes. How long will they take to fill it together?
questions.explanation: 1/20 + 1/30 = 5/60 = 1/12, so together they take 12 minutes.

questions.question: A train 150 m long passes a man running at 6 km/h in the same direction as the train in 10 seconds. What is the speed of the train?
questions.explanation: Relative speed = 150/10 = 15 m/s = 54 km/h. Train speed = 54 + 6 = 60 km/h.

questions.question: A boat's speed in still water is 12 km/h and the speed of the stream is 3 km/h. How long will it take to travel 45 km downstream?
questions.explanation: Downstream speed = 12 + 3 = 15 km/h. Time = 45/15 = 3 h.

questions.question: The diagonal of a cube is 6√3 cm. What is its volume?
questions.explanation: Diagonal = a√3 = 6√3 ⇒ a = 6 cm. Volume = 6³ = 216 cm³.

questions.question: A right circular cone has base radius 7 cm and slant height 25 cm. What is its volume? (Take π = 22/7)
If x = 3 + 2√2, what is the value of x + 1/x?
What is the measure of each interior angle of a regular hexagon?
questions.explanation: Each exterior angle = 360°/6 = 60°, so each interior angle = 180° − 60° = 120°.

questions.question: If sec θ + tan θ = 3, what is the value of sin θ?
questions.explanation: sec²θ − tan²θ = 1 ⇒ sec θ − tan θ = 1/3. Adding: 2 sec θ = 10/3 ⇒ sec θ = 5/3; tan θ = 4/3. sin θ = tan θ / sec θ = (4/3)/(5/3) = 4/5.

questions.question: What is the mode of the data 4, 6, 7, 6, 9, 4, 6, 3?
questions.explanation: 6 occurs three times, more than any other value (4 occurs twice), so the mode is 6.

questions.question: Thermometer : Temperature :: Barometer : ?
questions.explanation: A thermometer measures temperature; a barometer measures atmospheric pressure. (Humidity – hygrometer, wind speed – anemometer, rainfall – rain gauge.)

questions.question: Find the next number: 1, 4, 27, 256, ?
questions.explanation: The terms are nⁿ: 1¹, 2², 3³, 4⁴, so next is 5⁵ = 3125.

questions.question: Find the missing term: AB, DEF, HIJK, ?, STUVWX
questions.explanation: Groups of 2, 3, 4, 5, 6 consecutive letters, each separated by skipping one letter (C, G, L, R). After HIJK, skip L: MNOPQ; then skip R: STUVWX.

questions.question: If PAPER is coded as QBQFS, how will PENCIL be coded?
questions.explanation: Each letter is shifted one place forward: P→Q, E→F, N→O, C→D, I→J, L→M.

questions.question: In a certain code, FRIEND is written as HUMJTK. How will CANDLE be written in that code?
questions.explanation: Shifts are +2, +3, +4, +5, +6, +7: F→H, R→U, I→M, E→J, N→T, D→K. For CANDLE: C→E, A→D, N→R, D→I, L→R, E→L = EDRIRL.

questions.question: If '×' means '+', '−' means '×', '+' means '÷' and '÷' means '−', find the value of 20 + 5 − 3 × 8 ÷ 6.
A's father is B's only son. C is B's daughter, and D is C's son. How is D related to A?
questions.explanation: A's father is B's son and C is B's daughter, so C is A's paternal aunt. D, the son of A's aunt, is A's cousin.

questions.question:
Statements: Some engineers are doctors. No doctor is a lawyer.
Conclusions: I. Some engineers are not lawyers. II. Some lawyers are engineers.
Which conclusion(s) follow?
questions.explanation: The engineers who are doctors cannot be lawyers, so some engineers are not lawyers (I). Lawyers may or may not overlap with the other engineers, so II is uncertain.

questions.question: Which set of classes is best represented by three mutually intersecting circles?
questions.explanation: Some teachers are women, some are graduates, and some women are graduates – all three overlap. Lion and tiger lie inside Animal; pen, pencil, eraser are disjoint; Delhi ⊂ India ⊂ Asia.

questions.question: Select the odd one out: Kilometre, Metre, Centimetre, Litre
questions.explanation: Kilometre, metre and centimetre are units of length; litre is a unit of volume.

questions.question: A clock is placed so that at 12 noon its minute hand points towards the North-East. In which direction will its hour hand point at 1:30 p.m.?
questions.explanation: The '12' mark points North-East (45° clockwise from North). At 1:30 the hour hand is 45° past '12' (30° per hour × 1.5). So it points 45° + 45° = 90° from North, i.e. East.

questions.question: Six students E, F, G, H, I and J sit in a row facing north. E is third from the left end. I sits to the immediate left of E. G sits immediately between E and F. H sits at the right end. Who sits at the left end?
questions.explanation: E = 3, I = 2. G is between E and F, so G = 4 and F = 5 (position 2 is taken by I). H = 6, leaving position 1 for J.

questions.question:
Statement: A railway announcement says, 'Passengers are requested not to board moving trains.'
Assumptions: I. Boarding a moving train can be dangerous. II. Some passengers may try to board moving trains.
Which assumption(s) are implicit?
options: Neither I nor II is implicit
Both I and II are implicit
questions.explanation: The request is made because boarding moving trains is risky (I) and because some people do attempt it (II); otherwise the announcement would be pointless.

questions.question:
Question: On which day of the week is 10 March of a certain year?
Statement I: 6 March of that year is a Friday.
Statement II: 15 March of that year is a Sunday.
Which statement(s) are sufficient to answer the question?
options: I alone is sufficient, but II is not
II alone is sufficient, but I is not
Both I and II together are needed
Either I or II alone is sufficient
questions.explanation: From I: 6 March Friday ⇒ 10 March is 4 days later, Tuesday. From II: 15 March Sunday ⇒ 10 March is 5 days earlier, Tuesday. Each statement alone answers the question.

questions.question: In a row of 40 students, Ravi is 14th from the left end. What is his position from the right end?
questions.explanation: Position from right = 40 − 14 + 1 = 27.

questions.question: Which city will host the 2028 Summer Olympic Games?
questions.explanation: Los Angeles will host the 2028 Summer Olympics; Paris hosted in 2024 and Brisbane will host in 2032.

questions.question: From where did Mahatma Gandhi begin the Dandi March in March 1930?
questions.explanation: The Salt March started from Sabarmati Ashram, Ahmedabad, on 12 March 1930 and reached Dandi on 5 April 1930.

questions.question: Who presides over a joint sitting of the two Houses of Parliament?
questions.explanation: Under Article 118(4), the Speaker of the Lok Sabha presides over a joint sitting (summoned by the President under Article 108).

questions.question: Which type of soil is best suited for the cultivation of cotton?
questions.explanation: Black soil, formed from Deccan basalt, retains moisture and is ideal for cotton – hence also called black cotton soil.

questions.question: The Union Budget is presented as the 'Annual Financial Statement' under which Article of the Constitution?
questions.explanation: Article 112 provides for the Annual Financial Statement. Article 110 defines Money Bills, 280 the Finance Commission and 265 says no tax without authority of law.

questions.question: BrahMos, a supersonic cruise missile, has been developed jointly by India and:
questions.explanation: BrahMos is an India–Russia joint venture; its name combines the Brahmaputra and Moskva rivers.

questions.question: Bharatanatyam is a classical dance form that originated in which state?
questions.explanation: Bharatanatyam originated in Tamil Nadu. Kathakali and Mohiniyattam are from Kerala, Kuchipudi from Andhra Pradesh.

questions.question: The first Vande Bharat Express, flagged off in February 2019, ran between:
options: New Delhi and Shri Mata Vaishno Devi Katra
questions.explanation: The first Vande Bharat Express (Train 18) was flagged off on 15 February 2019 on the New Delhi–Varanasi route; New Delhi–Katra was the second.

questions.question: India's first indigenously designed and built aircraft carrier, commissioned into the Navy in September 2022, is:
questions.explanation: INS Vikrant (IAC-1), built by Cochin Shipyard, was commissioned on 2 September 2022. Vikramaditya was bought from Russia, Viraat was ex-British, and Arihant is a nuclear submarine.

questions.topic: Physics: Units, Motion & Laws of Motion
questions.question: Which of the following is a vector quantity?
questions.explanation: Velocity has both magnitude and direction. Speed, mass and time are scalars.

questions.topic: Physics: Units, Motion & Laws of Motion
questions.question: A ball is thrown vertically upward with a speed of 20 m/s. What maximum height does it reach? (g = 10 m/s²)

questions.topic: Physics: Units, Motion & Laws of Motion
questions.question: A stone is dropped from rest from a tall tower. What distance does it fall during the 3rd second of its motion? (g = 10 m/s²)
questions.explanation: Distance in nth second = u + (g/2)(2n − 1) = 0 + 5 × 5 = 25 m. (Check: 45 m in 3 s − 20 m in 2 s = 25 m.)

questions.question: The weight of an object on the Moon is about how much of its weight on the Earth?
questions.explanation: The Moon's surface gravity is about 1/6 of Earth's, so weight is about one-sixth (mass is unchanged).

questions.question: One kilowatt-hour (kWh) is equal to:
The twinkling of stars is due to:
questions.explanation: Starlight is refracted by layers of air with changing refractive index, so the apparent position and brightness fluctuate – twinkling.

questions.question: Myopia (short-sightedness) can be corrected by using a:
questions.explanation: In myopia the image forms in front of the retina; a diverging (concave) lens of suitable power corrects it.

questions.question: Resistors of 4 Ω and 12 Ω are connected in parallel across a 6 V battery. What is the total current drawn from the battery?
Fleming's left-hand rule is used to find the direction of:
options: Magnetic field around a straight wire
Force on a current-carrying conductor in a magnetic field
questions.explanation: The left-hand rule (motor rule) gives the force on a current-carrying conductor in a magnetic field. The right-hand rule gives induced current; the right-hand thumb rule gives the field around a wire.

questions.question: At what temperature do the Celsius and Fahrenheit scales show the same reading?
Isotopes of an element have the same:
questions.explanation: Isotopes have the same number of protons (atomic number) but different numbers of neutrons, hence different mass numbers.

questions.question: How many moles are present in 22 g of carbon dioxide? (C = 12, O = 16)
questions.explanation: Molar mass of CO₂ = 12 + 32 = 44 g/mol. Moles = 22/44 = 0.5.

questions.question: What is the chemical formula of bleaching powder?
questions.explanation: Bleaching powder is calcium oxychloride, CaOCl₂, made by passing chlorine over dry slaked lime.

questions.question: Which of the following non-metals is a good conductor of electricity?
questions.explanation: Graphite (an allotrope of carbon) has free electrons in its layers, so it conducts electricity, unlike most non-metals.

questions.question: The reaction Fe + CuSO₄ → FeSO₄ + Cu is an example of:
questions.explanation: More reactive iron displaces copper from copper sulphate solution – a displacement reaction.

questions.question: Which enzyme present in saliva begins the digestion of starch?
questions.explanation: Salivary amylase (ptyalin) converts starch into maltose in the mouth. Pepsin acts in the stomach, trypsin in the small intestine on proteins, lipase on fats.

questions.question: Who is known as the 'Father of Genetics'?
questions.explanation: Gregor Mendel's experiments on pea plants laid the foundation of the laws of inheritance.

questions.question: Which plant hormone is known as the 'stress hormone' and promotes closure of stomata?
questions.explanation: Abscisic acid (ABA) accumulates during water stress, causes stomatal closure and promotes dormancy; it is a growth inhibitor.

questions.question: What is the remainder when 5⁹⁹ is divided by 13?
What is the largest four-digit number that is exactly divisible by 88?
questions.explanation: 9999 ÷ 88 = 113 remainder 55. Largest multiple = 9999 − 55 = 9944 (= 88 × 113). 9856 is a multiple but smaller; 9988 and 9966 are not multiples.

questions.question: Simplify: (3½ − 1¾) × 2⅔
If √5 = 2.236, what is the value of 5/√5 + √20?
The HCF of two numbers is 16 and their LCM is 480. If one of the numbers is 96, what is the other number?
questions.explanation: Product of the numbers = HCF × LCM = 16 × 480 = 7680. Other number = 7680 ÷ 96 = 80.

questions.question: If A : B = 3 : 4, B : C = 6 : 7 and C : D = 14 : 15, what is A : D?
Six years ago the ratio of the ages of Ravi and Mohan was 5 : 7. Four years hence the ratio of their ages will be 7 : 9. What is Mohan's present age?
questions.explanation: Six years ago: 5x and 7x. Four years hence: (5x + 10)/(7x + 10) = 7/9 → 45x + 90 = 49x + 70 → x = 5. Mohan now = 7 × 5 + 6 = 41 years.

questions.question: A man spends 75% of his income. His income increases by 20% and his expenditure increases by 10%. By what percentage do his savings increase?
questions.explanation: Income 100, expenditure 75, savings 25. New income 120, new expenditure 82.5, new savings 37.5. Increase = 12.5/25 × 100 = 50%.

questions.question: A shopkeeper marks his goods 40% above the cost price and allows a discount of 15% on the marked price. What is his profit percentage?
What is the compound interest on ₹20,000 for 1½ years at 10% per annum, compounded half-yearly?
A sum of money lent at simple interest amounts to ₹7,440 in 3 years and to ₹8,400 in 5 years. What is the rate of interest per annum?

Pipes A and B can fill a tank in 12 hours and 15 hours respectively. Because of a leak at the bottom, the two pipes together take 10 hours to fill it. In how many hours can the leak alone empty the full tank?
questions.explanation: A + B fill 1/12 + 1/15 = 9/60 = 3/20 per hour. With the leak they fill 1/10. Leak rate = 3/20 − 1/10 = 1/20, so it empties the tank in 20 hours.

questions.question: A train crosses a 210 m long platform in 25 seconds and a man standing on the platform in 11 seconds. What is the speed of the train?
questions.explanation: Let speed = v m/s and length = L. L = 11v and L + 210 = 25v → 14v = 210 → v = 15 m/s = 15 × 18/5 = 54 km/h.

questions.question: A hemispherical bowl of internal radius 9 cm is full of liquid. The liquid is poured into cylindrical bottles, each of radius 1.5 cm and height 4 cm. How many bottles are needed to empty the bowl?
questions.explanation: Bowl volume = (2/3)π × 9³ = 486π cm³. Bottle volume = π × 1.5² × 4 = 9π cm³. Bottles = 486π ÷ 9π = 54.

questions.question: The perimeter of a rhombus is 52 cm and one of its diagonals is 24 cm. What is the area of the rhombus?
questions.explanation: Side = 52/4 = 13 cm. Half of the given diagonal = 12, so half of the other = √(13² − 12²) = 5 → other diagonal = 10 cm. Area = (24 × 10)/2 = 120 cm².

questions.question: If x + 1/x = 4, what is the value of x⁴ + 1/x⁴?
If sin θ + cos θ = √2 cos θ (θ acute), what is the value of tan θ?
questions.explanation: sin θ = (√2 − 1) cos θ, so tan θ = sin θ/cos θ = √2 − 1.

questions.question: From the top of a tower 60 m high, the angle of depression of a car on the ground is 30°. How far is the car from the foot of the tower?
questions.explanation: tan 30° = 60/d → d = 60/(1/√3) = 60√3 m (≈ 103.9 m). Using tan 60° by mistake gives 20√3 m.

questions.question:
Select the number that is related to the third number in the same way as the second number is related to the first number.
6 : 222 :: 7 : ?

Which number will replace the question mark (?) in the following series?
7, 12, 22, 37, 57, ?
questions.explanation: Differences are 5, 10, 15, 20, so the next difference is 25: 57 + 25 = 82.

questions.question:
Select the letter-cluster that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series.
AZ, CX, EV, GT, ?
questions.explanation: First letters move +2 (A, C, E, G, I) and second letters move −2 (Z, X, V, T, R). Next = IR.

questions.question: In a certain code language, NATION is written as OZUHPM. How will SCHOOL be written in that language?
questions.explanation: Letters are shifted +1, −1 alternately: N→O, A→Z, T→U, I→H, O→P, N→M. So S→T, C→B, H→I, O→N, O→P, L→K = TBINPK.

questions.question: In a certain code language, ROSE is written as 6821, CHAIR as 73456 and PREACH as 961473. How will SEARCH be written in that language?
questions.explanation: Each letter has a fixed digit: R = 6, O = 8, S = 2, E = 1, C = 7, H = 3, A = 4, I = 5, P = 9. SEARCH = 2 1 4 6 7 3.

questions.question:
If '÷' means '+', '+' means '×', '×' means '−' and '−' means '÷', what is the value of the following expression?
15 + 4 × 36 − 9 ÷ 6
If 4 @ 3 = 55 and 5 @ 2 = 121, then what is the value of 3 @ 4?
Pointing to a woman, Rohit said, 'Her father is the only son of my father's father.' How is the woman related to Rohit?
questions.explanation: The only son of Rohit's father's father is Rohit's father himself. So the woman's father is Rohit's father, and she is Rohit's sister.

questions.question:
Statements:
All engines are machines.
Some machines are tools.
No tool is a toy.
Conclusions:
I. Some machines are not toys.
II. Some engines are tools.
Which of the conclusions logically follow(s)?
questions.explanation: The machines that are tools cannot be toys, so I follows. Engines and tools are linked only through "some machines", so II is not definite. Only I follows.

questions.question:
Select the option that gives the most logical sequence of the following words.
1. Admission  2. Examination  3. Result  4. Study  5. Certificate
questions.explanation: A student first takes admission, then studies, appears in the examination, gets the result and finally the certificate: 1, 4, 2, 3, 5.

questions.question: In a survey of 200 people, 120 read newspaper A, 90 read newspaper B and 40 read both. How many people read neither newspaper?
questions.explanation: People reading at least one = 120 + 90 − 40 = 170. Neither = 200 − 170 = 30.

questions.question: Select the number that does not belong to the group.
questions.explanation: 169 = 13², 225 = 15² and 289 = 17² are squares of odd numbers; 324 = 18² is the square of an even number (and the only even number).

questions.question: Six persons L, M, N, O, P and Q sit in a row facing south. M sits at the extreme right end. Only two persons sit between M and O. N sits to the immediate left of O. Q sits to the immediate right of O. P sits at one of the ends. Who sits to the immediate left of M?
questions.explanation: Numbering positions 1–6 from their left: M = 6, O = 3, N = 2, Q = 4. P must take the other end, 1, so L = 5, i.e. immediately to the left of M.

questions.question: Five persons A, B, C, D and E live on different floors of a five-storey building (the ground floor is numbered 1 and the top floor 5). B lives on an even-numbered floor. C lives immediately above B. A lives on the top floor. D lives on a floor below E. Who lives on the ground floor?
questions.explanation: A = 5. If B = 4, C would be 5 – not possible, so B = 2 and C = 3. Floors 1 and 4 remain; D is below E, so D = 1 and E = 4.

questions.question: A man walks 7 km east, turns right and walks 3 km, then turns right again and walks 11 km. How far and in which direction is he from his starting point?
questions.explanation: He ends 11 − 7 = 4 km west and 3 km south of the start. Distance = √(4² + 3²) = 5 km, towards the South-West.

questions.topic: Physics: Units, Motion & Laws of Motion
questions.question: A body starting from rest moves with uniform acceleration and covers 20 m in the first 2 s. What distance does it cover in the first 4 s?
questions.explanation: s = ½at²: 20 = ½ × a × 4 → a = 10 m/s². In 4 s, s = ½ × 10 × 16 = 80 m (distance ∝ t², so doubling time gives 4 times the distance).

questions.topic: Physics: Units, Motion & Laws of Motion
questions.question: A force acting on a body of mass 2 kg for 0.1 s changes its velocity from 5 m/s to 15 m/s in the same direction. What is the magnitude of the force?
questions.explanation: F = change in momentum / time = 2 × (15 − 5)/0.1 = 20/0.1 = 200 N.

questions.question: A man of mass 60 kg climbs 20 steps, each 25 cm high, in 10 s. What is his power? (g = 10 m/s²)
The acceleration due to gravity on the Earth's surface is 9.8 m/s². What is its value at a height equal to the Earth's radius above the surface?
questions.explanation: g ∝ 1/r². At height R the distance from the centre is 2R, so g becomes 9.8/4 = 2.45 m/s².

questions.question: An object 4 cm high is placed 15 cm in front of a convex lens of focal length 10 cm. What is the size and nature of the image?
questions.explanation: 1/v = 1/f + 1/u = 1/10 − 1/15 = 1/30 → v = +30 cm. m = v/u = 30/(−15) = −2, so the image is 8 cm high, real and inverted.

questions.question: The refractive index of water is 4/3 and that of glass is 3/2 (both with respect to air). What is the refractive index of glass with respect to water?
questions.explanation: n(glass w.r.t. water) = n_glass / n_water = (3/2)/(4/3) = 9/8.

questions.question: How should three resistors of 4 Ω each be connected to obtain an equivalent resistance of 6 Ω?
options: Two in series, with this combination in parallel with the third
Two in parallel, with this combination in series with the third
questions.explanation: Two 4 Ω in parallel give 2 Ω; adding the third in series gives 2 + 4 = 6 Ω. The other options give 12 Ω, 4/3 Ω and 8/3 Ω.

questions.question: Two bulbs rated 100 W, 220 V and 60 W, 220 V are connected in parallel across 220 V mains. What is the total current drawn (approximately)?
questions.explanation: In parallel each bulb gets 220 V and works at its rated power. Total power = 160 W, so I = 160/220 ≈ 0.73 A.

questions.question: A person hears the echo of his clap from a cliff 1.5 s after clapping. If the speed of sound in air is 340 m/s, how far is the cliff?
questions.explanation: Sound travels to the cliff and back: 2d = v × t = 340 × 1.5 = 510 m, so d = 255 m.

questions.question: The ion X²⁺ contains 10 electrons and 12 neutrons. What is the mass number of the element X?
questions.explanation: X²⁺ has lost 2 electrons, so the neutral atom has 12 electrons = 12 protons. Mass number = 12 + 12 = 24 (magnesium).

questions.question: On moving from left to right across a period of the Modern Periodic Table, the atomic radius of elements generally:
questions.explanation: Across a period the nuclear charge increases while electrons enter the same shell, so the electrons are pulled closer and the atomic radius decreases.

questions.question: The sting of an ant or a nettle leaf injects which acid into the skin?
questions.explanation: Ant and nettle stings contain methanoic (formic) acid; a mild base such as baking soda gives relief.

questions.question: Which of the following metals does NOT liberate hydrogen gas from dilute hydrochloric acid?
questions.explanation: Copper lies below hydrogen in the reactivity series, so it cannot displace hydrogen from dilute HCl; Mg, Zn and Fe can.

questions.question: Which functional group is present in ethanoic acid?
questions.explanation: Ethanoic (acetic) acid, CH₃COOH, contains the carboxylic acid group –COOH.

questions.question: In the reaction ZnO + C → Zn + CO, which substance acts as the reducing agent?
questions.explanation: Carbon removes oxygen from ZnO (reducing it) and is itself oxidised to CO, so carbon is the reducing agent.

questions.question: Tuberculosis is caused by:
questions.explanation: Tuberculosis is caused by the bacterium Mycobacterium tuberculosis; the BCG vaccine protects against it.

questions.question: Which plant hormone mainly promotes cell division?
questions.explanation: Cytokinins promote cell division and are present in areas of rapid division such as fruits and seeds.

questions.question: In Mendel's cross between pure tall (TT) and pure dwarf (tt) pea plants, what is the genotypic ratio in the F₂ generation?
questions.explanation: F₁ is Tt. Selfing Tt gives TT : Tt : tt = 1 : 2 : 1 (the phenotypic ratio is 3 : 1).

questions.question: Which Indian state hosted the FIDE Chess World Cup 2025 (open section)?
questions.explanation: The FIDE World Cup 2025 was held in Goa from 31 October to 27 November 2025.

questions.question: Who was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize 2025?
questions.explanation: The Norwegian Nobel Committee awarded the 2025 Peace Prize to Venezuelan opposition leader María Corina Machado. Nihon Hidankyo won in 2024 and Narges Mohammadi in 2023.

questions.question: The 'PM Vishwakarma' scheme launched in September 2023 provides support mainly to:
questions.explanation: PM Vishwakarma offers recognition, skill training, toolkit incentives and collateral-free credit to artisans in 18 traditional trades.

questions.question: The Indian National Congress adopted the 'Purna Swaraj' (complete independence) resolution at its 1929 session held at:
questions.explanation: The Lahore session (December 1929), presided over by Jawaharlal Nehru, adopted the Purna Swaraj resolution; 26 January 1930 was observed as Independence Day.

questions.question: Which Constitutional Amendment Act lowered the voting age in India from 21 years to 18 years?
questions.explanation: The 61st Constitutional Amendment Act, 1988 amended Article 326 to reduce the voting age to 18 years.

questions.question: Which of the following rivers flows westward and drains into the Arabian Sea?
questions.explanation: The Narmada flows west through a rift valley into the Gulf of Khambhat (Arabian Sea). Godavari, Krishna and Mahanadi drain into the Bay of Bengal.

questions.question: Under the 'GST 2.0' rate rationalisation that came into effect on 22 September 2025, most goods and services fall under which two main slabs?
questions.explanation: The GST Council (56th meeting) merged the earlier 5/12/18/28% structure into two main slabs of 5% and 18%, with a special 40% rate for a few luxury/sin goods.

questions.question: Chandrayaan-3 was launched in July 2023 using which launch vehicle?
questions.explanation: Chandrayaan-3 lifted off on 14 July 2023 aboard LVM3-M4 from Sriharikota. PSLV-C57 later launched Aditya-L1.

questions.question: The Bairabi–Sairang railway line, inaugurated in September 2025, connected which state capital to the Indian Railways network for the first time?
questions.explanation: The 51-km Bairabi–Sairang line brought rail connectivity to Aizawl, capital of Mizoram, and was inaugurated on 13 September 2025.
